hostile.title: Operation Epic Fury opens: Pentagon says 1,000+ targets hit in the first 24 hours; Khamenei and ~40 senior officials killed; a strike near Minab hits a girls' school
US strikes hit Iran's navy from the first hours: drone carrier Shahid Bagheri attacked (CENTCOM); Bayandor and Naghdi reported sunk at Konarak (The War Zone)
IRGC radios ships on VHF that 'no ship is allowed to pass'; Iran does not formally confirm a closure order (Reuters, citing UKMTO and EU Aspides); IRGC-linked Tasnim says the Strait is shut
Iran fires missiles at Israel, Kuwait and other Gulf targets; a missile hits a residential block in Tel Aviv; Kuwait International Airport is hit by a drone

Iranian strikes on US/allied radar and base sites across the Gulf and Jordan; one THAAD AN/TPY-2 radar in Jordan 'apparently destroyed'; strikes on Manama, Kuwait airport, Abu Dhabi airport and Erbil reported the same day
Strike on a makeshift operations center at the port of Shuaiba, Kuwait
CENTCOM says the Iranian frigate Jamaran was struck at Chabahar at the start of Epic Fury and is 'sinking'; Makran struck at Bandar Abbas (USNI imagery), sinking not confirmed
Tanker Stena Imperative hit by suspected Iranian projectiles at a Bahrain port; smoke near the US embassy in Kuwait reported by a witness
IDF says it struck Iran's Supreme National Security Council complex in Tehran (Mar 2-3) and destroyed a secret underground site on Tehran's outskirts where Iran moved its nuclear work (IDF claim)
Two Iranian drones hit the US embassy in Riyadh; limited fire and minor damage per Saudi Defense Ministry (AP)
Iranian missile hits the US base at Al Udeid, Qatar (Mar 3); separately a drone attack on Saudi Aramco's Ras Tanura refinery causes a precautionary shutdown (Mar 2, Iran-attributed)
A US submarine sinks IRIS Dena ~40nm off Sri Lanka (reported as USS Charlotte by CBS citing unnamed officials; the Pentagon did not name it)

CENTCOM says US forces destroyed 16 Iranian minelayers near Hormuz on Mar 10; Trump said the US had 'no reports' of mines being laid. Pentagon: Iranian ballistic-missile launches down ~90%, drones ~83%

CENTCOM (Adm. Cooper, Mar 21) says the US has struck 8,000+ targets, including 130 Iranian vessels, since Feb 28. Iran's Tasnim says at least 16 cargo vessels burned at Bandar Lengeh/Kong after a US-Israeli attack (Mar 20)
Iran reports an attack on Natanz and blames the US and Israel; the Israeli military denied involvement and the IAEA saw no rise in off-site radiation
Iran strikes toward Dimona and Arad and calls it a 'response' to Natanz; Iran did not claim to target the Negev research center
Israel says it killed IRGC Navy commander Tangsiri and the IRGC Navy's intelligence chief Rezaei in Bandar Abbas (Israeli claim, Mar 26); Iran confirmed Tangsiri's death on Mar 30
Strikes Prince Sultan Air Base
Joint Chiefs Chairman Caine announces the first overland B-52 missions (NYT, Mar 31); strikes on an Isfahan ammunition depot reported separately by the WSJ (not read directly)
Destroys B1 bridge (Tehran-Karaj) during a family holiday gathering below
Iran shoots down a US F-15E over Iran (ABC); an A-10 is hit separately and crashes in an allied country, its pilot rescued
Israel strikes 100+ targets across Beirut, southern Lebanon and the Bekaa in about 10 minutes, within hours of the ceasefire (AP)
Iran restricts/resumes blockade, citing the Lebanon strikes as a ceasefire violation
UAE strikes Lavan Island oil refinery (only revealed later via WSJ/Bloomberg, May 11)
US Navy destroyers transit the Strait for the first time since the war began (mine-clearance framing)
US naval blockade of Iran begins
Iran announces the Strait closed again, citing continuation of the US blockade

US disables the Iranian container ship Touska with gunfire from USS Spruance (Apr 19, USNI); tankers Tifani and Majestic X interdicted in the Indian Ocean around Apr 22-24 (dates not confirmed by an allowed outlet)
IRGC seizes container ships MSC Epaminondas and MSC Francesca
Bubiyan Island raid attempt: 6 IRGC troops by fishing boat, 4 detained, 2 escape; Kuwait announced it on May 12
Operation Project Freedom: announced May 3, began May 4; Navy escort mission for stranded ships; US says six boats sunk (Trump said seven); pause announced May 5 US time (May 6 Gulf time)
Missiles, drones and small boats attack 3 US destroyers transiting the Strait
US strikes sites near Bandar Abbas and Qeshm Island (CENTCOM did not name the IRGC)
Strikes kill members of Iran's air-defense units
Downs a US Apache helicopter over the Strait (US says a Shahed drone did it)
Self-defense strikes on Qeshm Island, Sirik, Jask, Bandar Abbas radar/missile-defense sites
Strikes Muwaffaq Salti AB plus bases in Kuwait and Bahrain
Iranian missile wave at a Jordan base near Azraq; Jordan says it intercepted all 20 incoming missiles
US naval blockade of Iran officially ends
Israeli strikes in Lebanon continue overnight after an Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire took effect Jun 19 (Reuters, AFP)
Iran claims the Strait closed again, citing Israeli ceasefire violations in Lebanon
Drone attack on a cargo container ship in the Strait - first MOU violation, ~1 week after signing
~1 hour of retaliatory strikes on missile/drone sites and coastal radar
Tanker Kiku hit by a one-way drone near Hormuz (Jun 27, per CENTCOM; Iran has not confirmed); overnight Jun 27-28 the IRGC fires drones and missiles at Kuwait (intercepted) and Bahrain
Strikes three vessels in the Strait - second, larger MOU violation
90 targets across southern/northeastern Iran incl. two bridges - second consecutive night, marked jump in intensity
Iran's IRGC says it fired 10 ballistic missiles at the Azraq base in Jordan (Muwaffaq Salti AB is at Azraq); Jordan says it intercepted 8
Simultaneous strikes framed as retaliation for a '3rd round of US strikes within a week' (~140 sites)
Declares the Strait 'closed until the end of US interference'
Attack on Muwaffaq Salti AB - deadliest Jordan-strike day of the war
IRGC says ballistic missiles hit US aircraft at Aqaba airport (Jul 19); Jordan says it shot down 3 missiles and a 4th fell in open ground
Mine clearance of the Traffic Separation Scheme; 100+ suspected mines found and removed (Axios: by private contractors; CENTCOM credits Navy divers, SEALs and air power)
Strikes 2 IRGC rocket launchers on Larak Island, said to be preparing sea mines
'Punishment of the Aggressor': strikes King Hussein AB and Al Azraq AB

Saudi (Bahri) tanker Sidr hit late Aug 31; a second tanker, Senegal Prosperity, reported hit by 3 projectiles the same night. IRGC says mines; CENTCOM calls that false; Saudi Arabia blames Iran; Iran denies
New strike wave: Kenerak, Bandar Abbas, Qeshm Island
Kuhestak/Sirik wedding strike, part of the same wave as #73
Strikes Camp Titin and Prince Hassan AB
Strikes 3 Iranian crude tankers (MT Kylo and others)
IRGC fires ballistic missiles at a US warship for the second time in two days
CENTCOM destroys five IRGC crude oil carriers (four in the Gulf of Oman, one near Kharg Island) after the IRGC's missile attempts on a US warship
Strikes Muwaffaq Salti AB: 1 A-10 loses a wing, ~8 F-15s lightly damaged
At least 3 commercial vessels struck by projectiles in the Hormuz region; IRGC says 'military conflict' continues there daily
Cluster of projectile and drone attacks on tankers in and near Hormuz, Oct 2-5; Reuters' maritime security sources counted at least 12 tanker attacks in Sep 28-Oct 5, the most of any week of the war
Panama-flagged tanker On Peace hit by a projectile while crossing the strait; India condemns the attack (possibly Oct 5)
UKMTO reports a tanker struck off northern Qatar, well west of the strait
Unidentified projectile hits the laden supertanker GEM NO.2 at anchor off the UAE, outside the Hormuz area; fire put out (UKMTO)
IRGC Navy CLAIMS an unnamed supertanker on an unauthorised route hit a naval mine and caught fire, and threatens other tankers
CENTCOM releases footage of a fighter jet bombing the stern of a cargo ship it says was running the blockade of Iranian ports, disabling it (strike Oct 10 or 11)
UKMTO: an unidentified projectile hits an outbound tanker in the strait; separately the UAE coastguard rescues 22 crew from a tanker fire of unknown cause
US forces destroy an Iranian-affiliated dhow that CENTCOM says was 'conducting surveillance and targeting U.S. Navy ships' in the Gulf of Oman; crew removed first (announced Oct 14)
Singapore-flagged container ship GFS Pride hit by a projectile in the strait and sinks; a tanker is hit the same day (UKMTO). Iran said a mine sank it; CENTCOM said an IRGC projectile
Two tankers hit off Saudi Arabia, Oct 16-17: one by an unknown projectile, one by a rocket-propelled grenade from a small boat about 78 nautical miles northeast of Jubail

IRGC CLAIMS two supertankers, each carrying about 2 million barrels, hit naval mines on an 'unauthorised' route and caught fire (Oct 17-18); CENTCOM says the strait is cleared of mines and ships are being hit by projectiles
UKMTO: a tug is struck by two unknown projectiles off the UAE; damaged but continuing its route

options.name: Hold: no new action
options.what: Keep the current posture: blockade stays, no new strikes or sanctions.
risks: Ship crews: attacks on shipping continue at ~2.2 a week (e.g. On Peace, Oct 6: 12 crew injured). No new US act to answer.
No new US trigger. Iranian or unidentified attacks on shipping keep happening anyway (baseline). Whether holding back changes Iran's behaviour: not measured.
No added interceptor use from a US act; the blockade and patrols continue to cost what they cost now (not measured).
Baseline: ~2.2 attacks on shipping a week in the current phase. Oil prices and shipping costs: not measured.
Iran is expected to answer the US counter-offer; Trump's no-strike pledge stands until Nov 3. Strain with allies: not measured.
options.pros: No new US act for Iran to answer, so no added risk of retaliation from it. Keeps Trump's stated no-strike pledge before Nov 3. Leaves room for Iran's expected reply to the US counter-offer. Uses no interceptors.
options.harms: Attacks on shipping continue at about 1-2 a week (baseline), injuring crews (On Peace: 12 hurt) and raising shipping risk. Whether holding back weakens deterrence cannot be measured from this log.
options.unknown: Shipping attacks have kept coming without any new US move (see the baseline line). Trump has said there will be no US strikes before Nov 3; what Iran does if that holds is not in the data.

cases.title: US 15-point ceasefire plan is passed to Iran through Pakistani intermediaries (AP)

Trump announces a two-week ceasefire on Truth Social after Pakistan's PM Sharif asks him to extend his deadline; Iran's Supreme National Security Council accepts (Reuters, AP). Apr 7 US time / Apr 8 Gulf time
Islamabad Talks: 21 hours of negotiation, collapse without agreement
A ceasefire takes effect; Israel and Iran had not exchanged fire since

Trump and Pezeshkian sign a 14-point interim memorandum electronically on Jun 17 (Iran's foreign ministry calls it the 'Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding'): fighting stops on all fronts incl. Lebanon; 60 days to negotiate; the US starts lifting the blockade at once and ends it within 30 days; Iran makes 'best efforts' for free passage through Hormuz; oil-sanctions waivers now, full relief only in a final deal
US sends a formal counter-proposal via Qatari mediators responding to Iran's 7-day roadmap; US insists nuclear talks be included
Trump says on Truth Social the US 'will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections' (Nov 3), citing 'productive discussions'

risks: No direct casualties from the move itself.
Iran struck within 7 days after 2 of 7 past conciliatory US moves (timing only, not shown to be replies). Reply rate to diplomacy: not measured (not in the census).
No interceptor use expected from the move itself.
Attacks on shipping, 7 days before -> after past cases: 5 -> 9 (total). Oil prices and shipping costs: not measured.
Talks or diplomatic moves within 14 days after: 5 of 7. Strain with allies (Jordan, Gulf states, UK): not measured.
options.pros: No direct casualties. In the log, US diplomatic moves were usually followed by more diplomacy within two weeks (see measured column). A deal is the only option that addresses all the goals at once: the June memorandum included phased Hormuz reopening and an end to the blockade.
options.harms: Past deals did not hold: the April ceasefire was violated the same day, and the June deal collapsed on Jul 7 (Iran later said it never took effect). Shipping attacks continued during talks. Political costs of concessions are not measured here.
options.unknown: Diplomatic moves are not in the census, so there is no reply rate. The last rounds (Sep 23 - Oct 9) drew rejections and counter-offers, not attacks. Iran called the US answer 'insufficient' (Oct 11) and on Oct 18 said it was still reviewing US 'comments'.

cases.title: Treasury imposes new sanctions on 10 individuals/entities for supporting Iran's military supply chain

Treasury imposes sweeping new sanctions on Iran's automotive and rail industries and a shadow banking network tied to Russia - called 'some of the last significant elements' of Iran's IRGC-linked industrial base
Treasury sanctions 17 companies and 17 'shadow fleet' tankers carrying Iranian oil (Operation Economic Outcast)
Treasury sanctions 10 entities and 16 people in Iran's shadow-banking and exchange-house network, plus Iranian religious-charity networks; State sanctions a Cuban bank serving an Iranian bank

now.note: Analyst reading of the news, written by the weekly agent from logged events. Not data. Replace every week.
headline: Attacks on shipping are at a record: UKMTO counted 10-12 in the week to Oct 16, and the container ship GFS Pride sank on Oct 13 (#109). The US has not answered them with strikes on Iran.

Trump pledged on Oct 8 that the US 'will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to' the Nov 3 midterms (#97). CBS reports strike plans are ready (#111) and Trump has said action could resume after the midterms (#82, #88).
Talks are live: Iran says it is reviewing US 'comments' and that Hormuz would reopen on the sixth day if the US complies (#115). The US counter-offer went through Qatar on Sep 29 (#86).
Sanctions rounds keep coming roughly weekly (Sep 28, Oct 1, Oct 8, Oct 15), and the US disabled a blockade runner on Oct 10-11 (#104).

Midterm elections; end of Trump's no-strike pledge
Situation S002 window closes (what the US does Nov 4-17)
